assignment:
Your principal is reconsidering the school's cell phone policy. She is considering two possible policies: 
Policy 1: Allow students to bring phones to school and use them during lunch periods and other free times, as long as the phones are turned off during class time. 
Policy 2: Do not allow students to have phones at school at all.
Write a letter to your principal convincing her which policy you believe is better. Support your position with specific reasons.
essay_1:
Dear Principal,

I think Policy 1 is the best choice. Letting students have phones at lunch and free time, as long as they are off in class, is a great way to keep the good parts of phones and keep school fun and happy.

First, phones are a really good safety tool. If there is a late bus or a change in plans, students can reach their families right away, and parents feel safe and happy. Second, Policy 1 teaches responsibility. Students get to decide when a phone is okay to use. Learning to put a phone away and focus is a very useful skill for college and for work, and I love that we get to practice it now.

Third, the rule is simple and fair. Phones are off during class, and teachers can spend their time teaching, which is great for everybody. Lunch is also the one time we can relax, check on family, and laugh with friends. That nice rest helps us do well in the afternoon.

For these reasons, I hope you will choose Policy 1. Under a full ban, teachers would need a lot of time to check every bag in every room. Thank you for reading my letter.

Sincerely,
A Concerned Student
essay_2:
Dear Principal,

I think Policy 1 is the better choice. Letting us have our phones at lunch and in our free time, as long as they are off in class, is fair and the school can still run fine.

First of all, its about safety. If theres an emergency or the bus is late or my plans after school change, I need to be able to text my mom. If phones are banned all day parents are going to worry alot more.

Another reason is it teaches us responsibility. We have to decide when its ok to use a phone and when to put it away. We will need to do that in high school and at a job someday so we should get to practice now.

Also a full ban would be really hard to enforce. Teachers would waste time looking for phones and arguing with kids instead of teaching. Policy 1 is simple. Phones are off in class, and if you break the rule you lose your phone.

Lunch is the only time all day we can relax, talk to our friends, or check in with our family. I think that break helps us pay attention better in the afternoon classes.

So for these reasons, I hope you pick Policy 1.

Sincerely,
A Concerned Student
